stem: What is the typical prevalence of infantile hemangiomas by the time an infant reaches one year of age?
explanation: While only $1\%$-$2\%$ are present at birth, many more appear in the first few weeks, affecting about $10\%$ of infants by age one.
rationale: Consider how the prevalence grows from the newborn stage to the end of the first year.

optionExplanations.A: This is the prevalence range seen specifically in newborns, rather than the cumulative percentage at one year.
optionExplanations.B: While only $1\%$-$2\%$ are present at birth, many more appear in the first few weeks, affecting about $10\%$ of infants by age one.
optionExplanations.C: While common, the source specifies a lower prevalence rate of one in ten infants by the first birthday.
optionExplanations.D: Fifty percent refers to the proportion of hemangiomas that have typically involuted by age five, not the prevalence at age one.

source.hint: Consider how the prevalence grows from the newborn stage to the end of the first year.
